candidatesAccepted.title: Rivière-du-Loup to Rimouski along Route 132
candidatesAccepted.summary: A slower coastal drive with villages where the seven-year-old can stretch out. I have not checked which stops are open or accessible, and access needs were not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Rimouski to Matane, reaching the Gaspésie
candidatesAccepted.summary: Crosses into the Gaspésie with the river on one side, a natural place to break the drive. Access needs were not answered, so I have not checked whether the stops suit everyone.

candidatesAccepted.title: Matane to Sainte-Anne-des-Monts on Route 132
candidatesAccepted.summary: Continues along the Gaspé coast with frequent natural stops, which suits a party that wants to stop often. Access needs were not answered, so I cannot say what that changes.

candidatesAccepted.title: Sainte-Anne-des-Monts to Forillon at Cap-des-Rosiers
candidatesAccepted.summary: Brings you to Forillon National Park, one of the two stops you already want. Park entry costs and campground availability are not checked, and access needs were not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Forillon to Percé Rock along the Gaspé coast
candidatesAccepted.summary: Links the park to Percé Rock, your second stop, along the rocky shoreline. Boat tickets and park fees are not included in the band, the return to Montréal is not proposed here, and access needs were not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Simple motel room in Percé
candidatesAccepted.summary: A plain motel room in Percé keeps the rock and the town within walking distance and avoids campground nights entirely. I could not account for the party's access needs, which were not answered, so confirm step-free entry and ground-floor rooms before booking. Peak July rooms may sell out, and I have not checked availability or booking windows.

candidatesAccepted.title: Guesthouse room in Gaspé
candidatesAccepted.summary: A guesthouse in Gaspé is a simple, quiet base with a private bathroom, and it sits on the loop without a long drive to either stop. I have not checked whether it is open for the July dates, and access needs were not answered, so ask about stairs and bathroom layout before committing.

candidatesAccepted.title: Forillon campground with shower block
candidatesAccepted.summary: A campground in Forillon National Park is the simplest way to be near the park, but it only fits the party's limit if it has showers, which I have not verified. Access needs were not answered, so check whether the site and shower block are reachable for a child who tires easily and for any adult with mobility needs.

candidatesAccepted.title: Cabin near Forillon National Park
candidatesAccepted.summary: A rented cabin near Forillon gives the family a private, simple night with room to rest between stops, which suits a child who tires in the car. I cannot confirm the cabin's bathroom or access features, since access needs were not answered, and I have not checked rental dates in July.

candidatesAccepted.title: Rocher Percé viewing from the village
candidatesAccepted.summary: The rock is a stop you already want, and a short look from the village shore suits a seven-year-old better than a long push down the road. I did not check viewing-point hours, and the access needs were not answered, so those are still unknown.

candidatesAccepted.title: Bonaventure Island seabird boat trip
candidatesAccepted.summary: A boat trip to a seabird colony gives children something to watch and breaks up the driving. I did not check the operating season, boarding rules or prices, and the access needs were not answered, so anyone with mobility limits should ask about boarding first.

candidatesAccepted.title: Forillon National Park coastal walk
candidatesAccepted.summary: Short coastal walks and beach time at Cap-Bon-Ami let the children stretch in the middle of a half-day drive. I did not check trail lengths or park opening dates, and the access needs were not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Seafood lunch on the Percé waterfront
candidatesAccepted.summary: A relaxed sit-down seafood lunch in Percé, one of the stops the party already wants, gives the seven-year-old a break from the car. Access needs and dietary restrictions were not answered, so I could not check whether this suits everyone's eating needs; please confirm those before choosing a place.

candidatesAccepted.title: Picnic supplies from a Gaspé market
candidatesAccepted.summary: Buying bread, cheese, fruit and local smoked fish in Gaspé lets the party eat at a viewpoint or park when the children need to stretch, which suits a route with frequent stops. I did not check which shops are open or their hours, and dietary and access needs were not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Percé Rock from the village waterfront
candidatesAccepted.summary: A stop you already want, and it needs no ticket: the rock is visible from the village shore, so you can stop briefly and leave whenever the children tire. Access needs are not answered, so I cannot tell whether the shore paths and viewpoints suit everyone; please confirm before relying on this. Cost assumes only possible parking or incidental fees.

candidatesAccepted.title: Forillon National Park day visit
candidatesAccepted.summary: A stop you already want, with trails and coastal scenery you can take in gently at the children's pace. I have not checked current park fees or which trails are wheelchair or stroller accessible, and access needs are not answered, so treat the cost band as a rough assumption and confirm the entry fee.

candidatesAccepted.title: Bonaventure Island boat trip
candidatesAccepted.summary: A boat trip to a seabird colony offers something new compared with the north shore, and the children may enjoy it, though the crossing may be rough for the seven-year-old. I have not checked operating dates, schedules or accessibility, and access needs are not answered, so this is a proposal to verify rather than a confirmed option. Cost is a per-person assumption.

candidatesAccepted.title: Campground with showers near Forillon
candidatesAccepted.summary: A simple campground with showers would meet your rule against unshowered nights and suits a moderate-effort trip. I have not checked availability, shower facilities or whether sites suit a larger tent or vehicle, and access needs are not answered. The band is a per-party assumption for one night's pitch, not a quote.
